heroCommands.comment: Set up a palace for a project

heroCommands.command: mempalace search "why did we switch to GraphQL"

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: MemPalace is a local-first memory system for AI. It stores your conversation history and project files as verbatim text and finds them again with semantic search, so tools like Claude Code can recall past decisions. Nothing leaves your machine unless you opt in.
sixtySeconds.problem: AI coding sessions lose their context, and memory tools that summarise can distort what was said. MemPalace keeps the original text and organises it into wings (people and projects), rooms (topics) and drawers (content), reporting 96.6% recall at 5 on LongMemEval with no API calls.
whoFor: Claude Code, Gemini CLI and other agent users who want persistent memory
Developers who want searchable project history
Privacy-minded users who want memory that stays local
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for verbatim, local memory with no LLM required for retrieval. Watch out for impostor sites: the only official sources are the GitHub repository, the PyPI package and mempalaceofficial.com.
requirements: Python, installed with uv, pipx or a virtualenv
An MCP client to use it from an agent

overview: MemPalace mines content into a palace: project files, or Claude Code session transcripts with --mode convos. You can then search it, load context for a new session with wake-up, and audit how well organised it is. It doesn't summarise, extract or paraphrase what it stores.

Retrieval is pluggable. ChromaDB is the default and needs no configuration; SQLite, a native Rust engine, Milvus, Qdrant and pgvector are opt-in backends. The README's benchmarks are reproducible from the repository, and it explains why it avoids side-by-side comparisons with other memory projects.

Setup can be agent-guided: install the MemPalace skills and ask your coding agent to install the package, configure MCP and verify the connection. The README warns that Claude Code sessions expire in 30 days unless auto-save hooks are wired up, and links a retention checklist.

troubleshooting.solution: Install with uv tool install or pipx, or inside a virtualenv.
The image runs as uid 1000; mounted directories must be readable by it. Don't use --user.

troubleshooting.problem: First Docker command seems to hang
troubleshooting.solution: It's downloading the embedding model (about 80 MB by default) into /data.
Sessions expire in 30 days without auto-save hooks; follow the retention checklist.
